rows.grounds: compound: aśvamedha+phalam; accusative object of merit
compound: mahyam+arpaṇāt; offering directed to the deity

items.question: What merit results from offering to the deity in spring?
premises: An offering is made to the deity in spring.
Such an offering yields the fruit of the horse sacrifice.
items.inference: Therefore, spring offerings to the deity confer the merit of an aśvamedha.
items.plain_english: Offerings made to me in spring would yield the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

rows.grounds: compound: agniṣṭoma+phalam; accusative object of merit

items.question: What merit results from offering to the deity in summer?
premises: An offering is made to the deity in summer.
Such an offering yields the fruit of the agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
items.inference: Therefore, summer offerings to the deity confer the merit of an agniṣṭoma.
items.plain_english: O fair-complexioned one, offerings made in summer would yield the fruit of the agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

rows.grounds: compound: satra+yāga+phalam; accusative object of merit
compound: śaradi+arpaṇataḥ; seasonal offering as cause

items.question: What merit results from offering to the deity in autumn?
premises: An offering is made to the deity in autumn.
Such an offering yields the fruit of a satra sacrifice.
items.inference: Therefore, autumn offerings to the deity confer the merit of a satra sacrifice.
items.plain_english: Offerings made to me in autumn would yield the fruit of a satra sacrifice.

rows.grounds: compound: śatakratu+phalam; merit associated with Indra's sacrifice

items.question: What merit results from offering a karṇikāra flower in winter?
premises: A karṇikāra flower is offered in winter.
Such an offering yields the fruit of a hundred sacrifices.
items.inference: Therefore, offering a karṇikāra flower in winter confers the merit of a hundred sacrifices.
items.plain_english: A karṇikāra flower offered in winter would yield the fruit of a hundred sacrifices.

items.question: How is this offering regarded within the deity's worship?
premises: The offering is made in the deity's worship.
It is declared to be most excellent.
items.inference: Therefore, this offering holds the highest status in the deity's worship.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-faced one, this is declared to be the most excellent offering in my worship.

rows.grounds: act of worship as having infinite fruit

items.question: What fruit should be understood to arise from worship of the deity?
premises: Worship is directed to the deity.
Such worship yields infinite fruit.
items.inference: Therefore, one should know the deity's worship to be of infinite merit.
items.plain_english: O Pārvatī, one should know that worship of me yields infinite fruit.

rows.grounds: compound: nirmālyatā+doṣaḥ; defect of being used offering

items.question: Why may previously used offerings be employed continually in worship?
premises: There is no fault of staleness in these offerings.
Absence of fault permits their continued use.
items.inference: Therefore, one should always worship with them.
items.plain_english: Indeed, there is no fault of staleness in them; therefore one should always worship with them.

rows.grounds: compound: apavitra+jana+ānītam; brought by an impure person

items.question: What offering materials must be rejected due to their source?
premises: Leaves, flowers, or fruits may be brought by an impure person.
Materials from an impure source are unfit for worship.
items.inference: Therefore, one should reject leaves, flowers, or fruits brought by an impure person.
items.plain_english: One should reject a leaf, flower, or fruit brought by an impure person.

items.question: What defective flowers are prohibited from use in worship?
premises: A flower may be without a stalk or wounded.
Such defective flowers are unfit for worship.
items.inference: Therefore, stalkless or wounded flowers must not be used in worship.
items.plain_english: A flower without a stalk or with a wound is not to be used in worship.

rows.grounds: compound: patrāṇi+api; extends rule to leaves

items.question: How should leaves, especially the bilva leaf, be placed in worship?
premises: Leaves are to be placed in worship.
The bilva leaf should be placed facing downward.
items.inference: Therefore, one should place leaves likewise, with the bilva leaf facing downward.
items.plain_english: Leaves also should be placed likewise, and the bilva leaf should be placed facing downward.

rows.grounds: compound: bhasma+upari; position relative to ash

items.question: What placement rule governs sacred ash in relation to other offerings?
premises: Sacred ash should be placed above all other items.
Nothing should be placed above the sacred ash.
items.inference: Therefore, sacred ash must occupy the highest position in the arrangement.
items.plain_english: One should place sacred ash above all, and nothing should be placed above the ash.

items.question: What further instruction does the listener wish to hear after the brief summary?
premises: Everything has been stated in brief.
The listener may desire to hear more.
items.inference: Therefore, the speaker asks what the listener wishes to hear next.
items.plain_english: All has been said in brief; what then do you wish to hear?

rows.grounds: compound: raṅgavalī+ādi+kathanam; topic of the chapter

items.question: What is the title and position of this concluding chapter section?
premises: The section narrates raṅgavalī and related topics.
It is designated as the fourth chapter.
items.inference: Therefore, this is the fourth chapter named the narration of raṅgavalī and so forth.
items.plain_english: This is the fourth chapter, named the narration of raṅgavalī and so forth.

rows.grounds: compound: jagat+īśvara; vocative address to deity
compound: sarva+ātman; vocative address to deity

items.question: How does the speaker express reverence to the supreme deity?
premises: The deity is addressed as lord of the world and all-soul.
The speaker offers repeated obeisance.
items.inference: Therefore, the speaker repeatedly salutes the supreme deity.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the world, O all-soul, obeisance to you again and again.

items.question: What conduct is required of the practitioner during the time of worship?
premises: The practitioner acts at the time of worship.
Proper conduct during worship is to be explained.
items.inference: Therefore, the question asks how the practitioner should conduct himself during worship.
items.plain_english: How again should the practitioner conduct himself at the time of worship?

rows.grounds: compound: prāṇin+nirvāṇa+kāraṇam; cause of liberation for beings

items.question: What complete cause of liberation for beings is requested to be explained?
premises: The speaker requests a full explanation.
The explanation concerns the cause of liberation for beings.
items.inference: Therefore, the deity is asked to explain completely the cause of beings' liberation.
items.plain_english: Speak all of it completely, the cause of liberation for living beings.

rows.grounds: compound: phala+bhāg; one who obtains the fruit

items.question: What mental condition enables the worshipper to obtain the fruit of worship?
premises: The worshipper performs worship with the mind.
A pure mind makes the worshipper a sharer in the fruit.
items.inference: Therefore, only a worshipper with a pure mind obtains the fruit of worship.
items.plain_english: Only with a pure mind does the worshipper become a sharer in the fruit.

items.question: What reward does a devotee gain from performing abundant worship?
premises: A devotee performs abundant worship.
Abundant worship yields abundant prosperity.
items.inference: Therefore, a devotee engaged in abundant worship enjoys abundant prosperity.
items.plain_english: In abundant worship, the devotee enjoys abundant prosperity.

items.question: What posture and mental state are required for proper worship of the deity?
premises: The worshipper should be seated and restrained.
The worshipper should be single-minded.
items.inference: Therefore, one should worship the deity seated, restrained, and single-minded.
items.plain_english: Seated, restrained, and single-minded, one should worship me.

rows.grounds: compound: mūḍha+ātmā; one with confused mind
compound: pūjā+phala+bhāg; recipient of worship's fruit

items.question: Why does a deluded and restless person fail to obtain the fruit of worship?
premises: A deluded person acts with restless effort.
Restless delusion prevents attainment of worship's fruit.
items.inference: Therefore, a deluded and restless person does not become a sharer in the fruit of worship.
items.plain_english: But a deluded soul, restless with repeated effort, does not become a sharer in the fruit of worship.

items.question: Why does a fickle person who interrupts worship fail to gain its fruit?
premises: A fickle person summons others repeatedly in the middle of worship.
Such interruption prevents the worship from bearing fruit.
items.inference: Therefore, a fickle person who interrupts worship does not become fruitful.
items.plain_english: A fickle person who repeatedly summons others in the middle of worship does not obtain its fruit.

items.question: What inner state prevents a worshipper from approaching the deity's presence?
premises: A worshipper may be enraged by anger.
Anger obstructs access to the deity's presence.
items.inference: Therefore, a worshipper enraged by anger does not approach the deity's presence.
items.plain_english: A worshipper enraged by anger does not approach the deity's presence.

rows.grounds: compound: viṣaya+āsaktim; attachment to sense objects
compound: mat+arpitam; dedicated to the deity

items.question: What must be renounced and what must be done to align actions with the deity?
premises: Attachment to sense objects should be avoided.
Actions should be offered to the deity.
items.inference: Therefore, one should avoid sense attachment and make all actions an offering to the deity.
items.plain_english: One should avoid attachment to sense objects and again make everything an offering to me.

items.question: How should an offering be mentally dedicated to the deity after being placed near?
premises: The offering is first placed near.
It must then be offered with careful mental effort to the deity.
items.inference: Therefore, after placing the offering near, one should carefully offer it mentally to the deity.
items.plain_english: Then, having placed it near, one should carefully offer it to me with the mind alone.
